# Data dictionary

**NovaSpace Group synthetic dataset** — star schema, generated by [`../data-generator/generate.py`](../data-generator/generate.py) with a fixed seed (`numpy.random.default_rng(42)`).

Every table below serves at least one KPI in [`kpi-definitions.md`](kpi-definitions.md). Nothing here exists for decoration.

**Actual row counts and measured KPI values live in [`dataset-profile.md`](dataset-profile.md)**, which is generated by `data-generator/profile_dataset.py` rather than written by hand. This document describes the *schema*; that one reports what the seed actually produced. Figures quoted here are approximate by design — the profile is authoritative.

---

## Scope and volumes

| | |
|---|---|
| **Entities** | 4 (ES, FR, DE, UK) |
| **Fiscal calendar** | FY = calendar year (SAP fiscal year variant K4), periods 1–12 + special periods 13–16 |
| **Covered periods** | FY2023 P1 → FY2026 P6 — **42 closed periods**, plus special periods 13–14 in FY2023–FY2025 |
| **Group currency** | EUR |
| **Journal volume** | ≈ 1.12 M lines (≈ 26.7 k per month across all entities) |
| **Group scale** | ≈ €940 m revenue and €895 m cost per year, at a ~5 % margin |

The group's size is a consequence of the posting volume, not a separate choice: ~320 k journal lines a year describes a company of roughly €1 bn revenue. An earlier calibration put the average line an order of magnitude higher, which implied a €14 bn group running a 40 % annual loss on 196 cost centres — internally inconsistent in three directions at once. Amount medians are set so that the ledger, the cost-centre count, the programme portfolio and the P&L all describe the same company.

FY2026 is deliberately **incomplete** (closed through P6, today being 2026-07-25). Without a partial current year, KPI-05's EAC has no remaining periods to extrapolate into and forecast accuracy has nothing left to be wrong about.

## Naming and type conventions

- Table names `DIM_*` / `FACT_*`, upper snake case — the shape a HANA schema expects.
- Column names lower snake case. Dates are `DATE` (ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`), never strings.
- Amounts are `DECIMAL(15,2)`. **Never floats.** Binary floating point and money do not belong in the same column.
- Booleans are emitted as `true` / `false` in CSV and typed `BOOLEAN` in HANA.
- Nullable columns say so explicitly. Empty string is not null; the loader distinguishes them.
- **No derived analytical flags are stored in the facts.** `is_manual_posting`, `is_late_posting` and signed amounts are computed in the L2 harmonised layer. L1 is 1:1 with these tables, as [`../hana/README.md`](../hana/README.md) requires.

| company_code | company_name | country | local_ccy | soft_close_wd | hard_close_target_wd |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NS10` | NovaSpace España S.A. | ES | EUR | 4 | 5 |
| `NS20` | NovaSpace France S.A.S. | FR | EUR | 4 | 5 |
| `NS30` | NovaSpace Deutschland GmbH | DE | EUR | 4 | 5 |
| `NS40` | NovaSpace UK Ltd. | GB | **GBP** | 4 | 5 |

**Two stories are deliberately assigned to different entities.** NS30 is the chronically slow closer; NS40 is the only non-EUR entity and therefore the only source of FX impact. Putting both traits on one entity would entangle KPI-01 with KPI-06 and neither dashboard page could then be read cleanly. Every entity has the *same* close targets — the slowness is in the actuals, not in a softer target, so it shows up as a miss rather than as a different rule.

| programme_id | name | type | lead | start | end | relative size | derived budget (€M) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| `PRG-HELIOS` | Helios-3 Earth Observation Constellation | SATELLITE | NS10 | 2023-01 | 2027-12 | 210 | 690.3 |
| `PRG-KESTREL` | Kestrel Launcher Development | LAUNCHER | NS20 | 2023-01 | 2027-12 | 185 | 635.2 |
| `PRG-AURORA` | Aurora Deep-Space Relay | SATELLITE | NS30 | 2023-04 | 2028-06 | 96 | 406.7 |
| `PRG-TERRA` | TerraScan Ground Segment | GROUND_SEGMENT | NS40 | 2023-01 | 2026-12 | 58 | 153.4 |
| `PRG-MERIDIAN` | Meridian Navigation Payload | SATELLITE | NS20 | 2023-07 | 2027-06 | 74 | 221.5 |
| `PRG-CASTOR` | Castor Smallsat Platform | SATELLITE | NS10 | 2024-01 | 2027-12 | 42 | 149.4 |
| `PRG-PHAROS` | Pharos Optical Comms Demonstrator | TECHNOLOGY | NS30 | 2023-01 | 2025-12 | 19.5 | 13.3 |
| `PRG-VESTA` | Vesta Propulsion Test Bench | TECHNOLOGY | NS20 | 2023-01 | 2026-06 | 27 | 63.8 |
| `PRG-LYRA` | Lyra Constellation Operations | GROUND_SEGMENT | NS40 | 2024-07 | 2029-12 | 88 | 336.5 |
| `PRG-BOREAS` | Boreas Polar Weather Satellite | SATELLITE | NS30 | 2025-01 | 2029-12 | 130 | 467.5 |

**Why the budget is derived rather than declared.** *Relative size* is a configured input: it decides how many cost centres each programme attracts, so the generated spend comes out in roughly the intended proportions. It cannot also be the euro budget, because total spend is set by posting volume and amount medians, which know nothing about a number typed into a config file.

When the two were left disconnected, every programme sat at several times its stated lifetime budget and the *smallest* programme looked like the worst overrun — so KPI-05 ranked a perfectly healthy programme as the problem and the actual runaway second. `total_budget_eur` is therefore computed after the journal exists, from each programme's own baseline burn × planned duration × a 5 % plan cushion. For the overspending programme, "baseline" means the period *before* the overrun started, which is exactly what its budget would have been built from in reality.

Result: nine programmes land at 95–98 % of budget on EAC, and `PRG-KESTREL` at **126.6 %**. See [`dataset-profile.md`](dataset-profile.md).

**`PRG-KESTREL` is the overspending programme** — burn accelerates from FY2025 P7 onward. Launcher development is the realistic place to put an overrun, and it sits in NS20, a third entity distinct from the slow closer (NS30) and the FX entity (NS40). Three stories, three entities, no interference.

All names are invented. No real space programme, past or present, is referenced.

## RATES — 288 rows

Monthly FX to group currency, at two rate types. Both are needed: KPI-06 is precisely the difference between them.

| Column | Type | Null | Description | Sample |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `from_currency` | NVARCHAR(3) | no | **PK part** | `GBP` |
| `to_currency` | NVARCHAR(3) | no | **PK part.** Always `EUR` | `EUR` |
| `fiscal_year` | INTEGER | no | **PK part** | `2025` |
| `fiscal_period` | INTEGER | no | **PK part.** 1–12 | `7` |
| `rate_type` | NVARCHAR(1) | no | **PK part.** `M` = monthly average actual, `B` = budget/constant rate held flat for the FY | `M` |
| `exchange_rate` | DECIMAL(15,6) | no | Multiply `from` by this to get `to` | `1.183400` |

Currencies: `EUR`→`EUR` (always 1.0), `GBP`→`EUR`, `USD`→`EUR`. 3 currencies × 48 months × 2 rate types = 288 rows.

GBP drifts through the covered period; the `B` rate is frozen at each fiscal year's opening rate. The gap between the two *is* the FX impact.

### Document types

| Code | Description | Manual? | Timing behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SA` | G/L account document | **yes** | Clusters in working days 1–5 after period end |
| `SB` | G/L accrual posting | **yes** | Clusters at period end; reversed the following period |
| `KR` | Vendor invoice | no | Spread through the period |
| `RE` | Invoice receipt (logistics) | no | Spread through the period |
| `RV` | Billing document | no | Weighted to period end |
| `ML` | Payroll posting | no | **Punctual** — fixed working day each period |
| `AF` | Depreciation posting | no | **Punctual** — period end |
| `KA` | Allocation / assessment cycle | no | **Punctual** — close working day 3 |
| `WA` | Goods issue | no | Spread through the period |
| `IC` | Intercompany charge | no | Weighted to period end |

`is_manual_posting := document_type IN ('SA','SB')` — derived in L2, not stored.

**Vendor payments (`KZ`) are deliberately absent.** A payment clears accounts payable against bank — both balance-sheet accounts, and this dataset carries only P&L accounts. Including `KZ` would have meant posting it to a P&L account it never touches in reality, which is the kind of detail that reads as wrong to anyone who has worked in FI. Its share is redistributed across `KR`, `RE` and `WA`.

### Sign convention

Amounts are stored **unsigned** with direction in `debit_credit_ind`, as SAP does. The L2 layer derives:

```
signed_amount = CASE WHEN debit_credit_ind = 'S' THEN amount ELSE -amount END
```

Under this rule expenses are positive and revenue negative. Every KPI formula in [`kpi-definitions.md`](kpi-definitions.md) assumes signed amounts from L2 upward.

### Currency translation, and the one case where it does not reconcile

Amounts are translated outward along the real chain — document → local → group — with rounding at each hop. Deriving the group amount from the *rounded* local amount is what makes `amount_group = round(amount_local × rate, 2)` exactly true, which the L2 layer relies on when it re-derives group currency independently.

**Reversals are the exception, deliberately.** A reversal posts the amounts of the document it reverses, in all three currencies, exactly as `FB08` behaves. Since it lands in the following period, it does *not* reconcile at that period's rate. For the GBP entity this is visible, and it is precisely the exposure the FX revaluation task (`T09`) exists to deal with. Silently re-translating reversals would erase a real effect and make the FX story cleaner than the world is.

### Built-in data stories

The generator produces these on purpose. The tests in [`../data-generator/tests/`](../data-generator/) assert each one is actually present, because a story that was intended but not generated is worse than no story.

| # | Story | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **NS30 closes chronically late** | Higher manual-posting share, entry dates pushed 2–4 working days later, hard close missed most periods |
| 2 | **PRG-KESTREL overspends** | Burn multiplier ramps from FY2025 P7, reaching ~1.4× planned run-rate |
| 3 | **FX distorts NS40** | GBP drifts against a frozen budget rate, so group-currency variance ≠ local-currency variance |
| 4 | **~2 % of IC pairs mismatch** | Partner-side amounts perturbed or the mirror line dropped, concentrated where entity close dates diverge |
| 5 | **Special periods 13–14 are used** | Year-end adjustment entries in FY2023–FY2025, `SA`/`SB` types, posted in January of the following year |
| 6 | **Manual entries spike at close** | `SA` volume concentrated in working days 1–5 after period end, with a late tail |

Measured on the published seed:

| # | Story | Measured result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Slow closer | **8.2** working days to close vs 5.1–5.4 for the other three |
| 2 | Overspend | EAC at **126.6 %** of budget; the other nine sit at 95–98 % |
| 3 | FX | **−€4.4 m**, 0.67 % of the entity's cost base; euro entities exactly €0 |
| 4 | IC mismatch | **5 of 252** pair-periods (2.0 %); reconciling pairs net to **€0.00** exactly |
| 5 | Special periods | **12,970** lines, 1.16 % of the journal |
| 6 | Manual spike | Manual share **22.4 %** for NS30 vs 13.3 %; late postings **9.1 %** vs 2.2 % |

The overspend ramps to **1.65×** baseline over nine months, not the 1.4× over twelve first tried: that averaged to roughly +9 % across the first fiscal year, sat inside the budget noise, and left the programme not actually breaching its budget. The story existed in the generator's intent and not in the data.

Mismatches are injected **per reconciling pair-period, not per line**. The distinction is not cosmetic — a pair-period holds hundreds of intercompany documents at full volume, so a 2 % per-*line* rate leaves almost every pair containing at least one broken line, and 89 % of pairs failed to reconcile. The reduced-scale test run could not see it; it surfaced only against the full dataset.

| `actual_completion_date` | DATE | yes | **Null = not completed.** Must be reported as open, never as zero | `2025-04-11` |
| `completed_by_user_id` | NVARCHAR(12) | yes | Pseudonymised | `USR-77B2E1` |
| `delay_working_days` | INTEGER | yes | Working days between due and actual. Negative = early | `2` |

---

## Personal data

`posting_user_id`, `manager_user_id` and `completed_by_user_id` are **pseudonymous tokens generated directly** — format `USR-` + 6 uppercase hex characters, drawn from the seeded RNG. There is no name anywhere in the pipeline to pseudonymise *from*: no real or fake person's name is ever generated, mapped or stored, so no re-identification key exists to leak.

This is stricter than production pseudonymisation, where a reversible mapping is held separately by design. The relevant point for [`gdpr-and-data-protection.md`](gdpr-and-data-protection.md) is that these tokens do not reach the L3 reporting layer at all — user-level attribution is an audit function, not a management-reporting one.

## Referential integrity

The generator guarantees, and the test suite asserts:

- Every FK value in every fact exists in its dimension.
- `programme_id` is null or valid — never an empty string, never an orphan.
- Every journal line's `(fiscal_year, fiscal_period)` falls inside the covered range, and periods 13–16 appear only in FY2023–FY2025.
- `entry_date >= document_date` and `posting_date >= document_date` on every line.
- Every `RATES` lookup a journal line needs exists for its `(currency, fiscal_year, fiscal_period)`.
- Intercompany lines always carry a non-null `ic_partner_company`, and it never equals `company_code`.

## Known simplifications

Stated so they read as decisions, not as things that were missed:

- **One group-wide holiday calendar** rather than per-country calendars. Real Spanish, French, German and UK calendars diverge substantially, which would make working-day counts entity-specific. This would make the model more realistic and KPI-01 harder to compute — a fair trade, deferred to the backlog rather than pretended away.
- **No balance-sheet accounts.** P&L only. A close cockpit that ignores the balance sheet is incomplete in reality; here it keeps the account hierarchy legible.
- **Budget phased evenly across 12 periods.** Real budgets are phased on an activity profile. The even rule is stated wherever the comparison is made.
- **No commitments or open POs**, which is why KPI-05's EAC is explicitly labelled an early-warning indicator rather than a forecast.
- **Fiscal year = calendar year.** Non-calendar fiscal year variants are common and would add period-shifting logic that teaches nothing extra here.
